# Narracore Format

**Free, local, unlimited screenplay formatting for AI agents.** An open-source MCP server
(and DSH p

lugin) that turns raw or loosely
formatted screenplay text into professionally structured screenplay

blocks and typeset plain
text — **Chinese, English, or mixed — including Japanese broadcast-drama f

ormat and Chinese
colon-style dialogue scripts. The layout engine picks the right track automaticall

y: a
33-char × 38-line CJK grid or a 61 × 55 Latin grid**, the same fixed typewriter character
grid

8-line CJK grid or a 61 × 55 Latin grid**, the same fixed typewriter character
grid as narracore.cn.

- **Free forever** — runs on your machine, no account, no key, no quota, no network calls
- **Determ

inistic** — pure rule-based engine, no LLM inside; same input always yields the
same output, byte fo

r byte
- **Agent-native** — machine-readable diagnostics, evidence-anchored scene scoring,
typed-blo
cks chaining contract across tools

Part of the Narracore toolkit — the
long-form co-writing workbench. Looking for print-ready **PDF ex

port** or the full
story-continuity tooling? See the ecosystem below.

ransition / shot / note), page stats, and machine-readable diagnostics — feed

ny other tool in this package for analysis or conversion.

That's it. Your agent gets five tools under the `mcp__narracore__*` namespace.
### Any MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, …)
The package is a standard stdio MCP server, so any MCP client can run it directly:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Requires Node ≥ 22.
## Tools (5)
| Tool | What it does |
| `format_screenplay` | Parse screenplay text (or typed blocks) into 8 semantic block types, typeset
plain text, page stats, and diagnostics. `output="validate_only"` checks structure without formatti

ng. |
| `analyze_screenplay` | Deterministic statistics: scene list with structured headings (number
/ location / time of day / INT-EXT), per-scene word count, dialogue ratio, action density, characte

r share table. |
| `diagnose_scenes` | Scene-level "shootability" diagnosis: the agent cites evidenc
e per scene, the tool validates it verbatim and computes exact 0–100 scores (severity-weighted cover

age, BigInt arithmetic — never fakes a score). |
| `convert_fountain` | Convert between Narracore ty

ped blocks and Fountain, the plain-text screenplay interchange format. |
| `about_narracore` | Ecosy
stem overview — what else Narracore offers. |

**Chaining contract:** to run another tool on the same screenplay, pass back the `blocks`
you receiv

ed (`input_format="blocks"`), not the formatted plain text — blocks parse
deterministically; text re

ut_format="blocks"`), not the formatted plain text — blocks parse
deterministically; text re-parses.
## Ecosystem

- **narracore.cn** — the full long-form
co-writing workbench this toolkit comes from: screenplay and

story writing with the same
typesetting, plus story-window continuity tooling that goes beyond a lo

cal formatter.
- **narracore.app** — the hosted MCP
service built on the same pipeline, adding a pri

nt-ready **PDF export** with embedded
fonts (cover page, running headers, signed download links). Yo

u can buy N uses of the
formatting service there if you want the PDF pipeline without installing any

buy N uses of the
formatting service there if you want the PDF pipeline without installing anything.
## Engine provenance

The layout engine in `src/format/` is the same single source of truth used by narracore.cn.
It is po

rted verbatim from the Narracore codebase (provenance hashes in
`src/format/README.md`), and **snaps

hot tests pin it byte-for-byte** —
green snapshot tests are the machine proof that this package lays

out text identically to
the narracore.cn web app. The analysis layer (`src/analysis/`) is a TS port

of the Narracore
analyzer, locked by golden tests generated from the original implementation.
